samples.summary: `emailAt`'s "don't re-link a rejected URL's tail" guard only checks for `/`, so `https://user:pw@evil.example/x` still paints a `mailto:pw@evil.example` link over the userinfo of a URL that `toUrl` just refused
samples.evidence: `emailAt` refuses an address whose local part is preceded by `/` (line 400) precisely so that the tail of a userinfo URL is not re-linked. For `https://user:pw@evil.example/x` the backward walk stops at `:` (not in EMAIL_LOCAL_CHAR), so `start` points at `p`, `text[start-1] === ':'` passes both guards, the domain `evil.example` is a valid hostname, and `toUrl` yields `mailto:pw@evil.example`. A span is therefore painted over `pw@evil.example` inside a URL the scheme branch deliberately rejected as deceptive. The new test `refuses userinfo in credentials` (cell-links.test.ts) only asserts `urls(...).filter(/^https?:/)` is empty, so it passes while a link is in fact emitted. The same hole yields a mailto span for `www.paypal.example@evil.example/x`, whose painted text begins with a trusted-looking host while the destination is a different one.

samples.summary: The hover-card "gap between two links" fallback resolves the pointer to a cell ref, which disagrees with the painter's `sref` for merged cells and overflowing text — the card closes while crossing plain text in exactly the wide cells the feature targets
samples.evidence: `updateLinkHover` falls back to `toSref(this.toRefFromMouse(x, y))` when no span is hit, then requires `linksInCell(candidate)` to be non-empty. But the painter records links under the merge *anchor*'s sref, and text overflowing into empty neighbours is painted (and recorded) under the originating cell's sref. When the pointer sits in the gap between two links but over a covered sub-cell of a merge (e.g. D5 inside a C5-anchored merge) or over an overflowed neighbour column, `candidate` is that other ref, `linksInCell` returns [], `sref` becomes null and the card is closed — the exact strobe the fallback was added to prevent, in exactly the wide/multi-link cells the comment at lines 961-966 says the feature exists for.

samples.summary: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(url)` throws a TypeError when `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (insecure origin, older browser), which the handler's rejection path does not catch
samples.evidence: The click handler handles a *rejected* write (`.then(ok, err)`) but not an absent Clipboard API: on a non-secure origin `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`, so `navigator.clipboard.writeText` throws synchronously inside the React event handler and is never reported to the user — the very case the surrounding comment ("an insecure origin, a lost focus, a cross-origin frame") says it is guarding. A `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(url)?.then(...)` or try/catch would close it.

samples.summary: The host's close delay (250ms) is shorter than the engine's open delay (300ms), so returning to the same link cell from the card always blanks the card before it reopens
samples.evidence: `scheduleLinkHoverClose` fires at 250ms; `LinkHoverDelayMS` in worksheet.ts is 300ms, and entering the card triggers the grid's `mouseleave` -> `resetLinkHover()` (worksheet.ts:3591), which forgets `hoveredLinkSref`. So when the pointer leaves the card back onto the same cell, `onPointerLeave` schedules a close at 250ms while the engine cannot re-emit before 300ms: the card is guaranteed to disappear and reappear. The two constants live in different packages with no relation expressed between them.

samples.summary: The scheduled hover callback captures `urls` at schedule time; a repaint during the 300ms delay (collaborator edit, recalc) emits a card built from URLs that are no longer painted
samples.evidence: `this.linkHoverTimer = setTimeout(() => this.onLinkHoverCallback?.({ sref, urls }), LinkHoverDelayMS)` closes over the `urls` array read before the delay. `updateLinkHover` only runs on mousemove, so if the grid repaints while the pointer is stationary the timer still emits the stale list — the same staleness the `same`-comparison at lines 985-991 was added to avoid for the already-open case.

finding.summary: Non-ASCII characters in a URL path truncate the span, so the link navigates to a wrong (truncated) destination instead of not linking
finding.evidence: `URL_CHAR` (line 36) contains only RFC 3986 ASCII characters. A pasted URL with a non-ASCII path — common in exactly the Korean Confluence/Notion sheets the fixtures in `cell-links.test.ts` are drawn from, e.g. `https://wiki.example.com/x/기획문서` — stops the forward walk at the first Hangul byte. `detectLinks` then emits a span of `https://wiki.example.com/x/`, which parses and passes `isSafeUrl`, so a *truncated* URL is painted, recorded as a hit box and handed to `window.open`. The same file argues the opposite policy for the length bound (line 293: "linking a truncated destination is worse than linking nothing"), and that reasoning is not applied here. No test covers a non-ASCII path.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist as claimed. `detectLinks` does not terminate the forward walk at `URL_CHAR` alone: line 462-467 passes the ASCII run end through `extendPath`, which (lines 316-329) continues the span across non-ASCII letters/numbers/marks/surrogates (`isPathChar`, lines 58-62) once the authority has reached a path (`search(/[/?#]/)` gate, line 323). Tracing the finding's exact example `https://wiki.example.com/x/기획문서`: the run stops at `기`, `isPathChar('기')` is true, `slice(8,26)` = `wiki.example.com/x/` contains `/`, so the walk resumes and the full URL is emitted — no truncated span is produced. The claim that no test covers a non-ASCII path is likewise false: `cell-links.test.ts` lines 306-340 contain a `non-ASCII paths` describe block asserting the whole-URL span for that very Korean string (313-317), a CJK query (319-322), an astral path character (324-327), and the complementary host-stays-ASCII / IDN-homograph refusals (329-339).
